question: When creating extra viewpoints from light-field camera data, why might it work better to measure training error on images combined from many views rather than on each view separately?
answer: Measuring the error on images that are formed by combining many views (e.g., refocused images) is more effective because the light‑field is ultimately perceived as a single integrated image rather than as a set of isolated viewpoints.  Traditional view‑synthesis losses that evaluate each view independently ignore how the synthesized views will behave when they are composited into a refocused picture, which can lead to artifacts that are not captured by per‑view metrics.  By training on a loss computed on the combined, refocused image (the “refocused image error”), the network is encouraged to produce a light field whose overall refocused quality is high, yielding better visual results than optimizing each view separately [1].
